task: Find one-way flights from Zurich to London on October 22, 2026, for one adult in economy. Stop when matching flight options are visible. Do not select or book a flight.
scope: Three alternating untraced/traced pairs, untraced first, of one task in one existing Chrome profile. Each run opens and closes its own background tab. All six attempts of this series are included; none was repeated or replaced. A first series of six, all verified, exposed a run-file defect that left a stale attempt and no final save; after the fix in agent.py all six were run again, and these are the measurement (first series under superseded_series). Timing: first prediction after the initial homepage observation through the accepted DONE; setup and the independent post-run verification are excluded. The traced arm passes trace_path, so Agent.save() writes run.json during the run and once more at the stop.

gate.rule: traced median elapsed_ms within 10% of untraced median
gate.result: failed as written: the traced median took 19.7% less time, outside ±10%
gate.waiver: waived on the user's behalf, because tracing costs about 0.2% per run and the spread came from provider latency

run_file_checks.rule: run.json parses, attempt is null, status is done, final decision is DONE, decisions and history match state.json

save_microbenchmark.saves_rule: in the timed window: 2 per executed step (before input, after logging) and 2 per stale drop that had saved its attempt (before input, after clearing it); 1 more at the stop, after timing
save_microbenchmark.note: Pure write cost: the real Agent.save() and the bare write in isolation, 200 times each, written to a scratch directory outside the repository.

tracing_cost.measure: in-run leftover: elapsed_ms minus TypeSafe request, text-helper and browser-protocol (CDP) call time
tracing_cost.note: Every run executed 10 steps and no WAIT.

latency_probe.design: Ten request bodies with more than 20 questions from the first series' state.json files (runs 1-6), each sent once as recorded and once with every commit_* question removed, alternating which went first, through jev_ultrafast.model.post_json and its client; then five 1-question Choice requests on a tiny state. 25 HTTP requests; post_json's internal retry was refused, never sent.

requests.error: Refused: post_json wanted a retry after HTTP 529; refused (budget)

latency_probe.commit_question_latency_effect: not resolved (paired median +0.25 s, 6 of 9 pairs slower, range −0.85 to +1.2 s); input tokens +82%
latency_probe.one_question_vs_full: 1-question requests were no faster (median 4.4 s vs 3.6 s for full requests)

superseded_series.reason: Run-file defect: a stale-dropped step left its pre-input attempt in run.json and the stop did not save, so traced run files ended with a non-null attempt and without the final DONE decision.
superseded_series.scope: Three alternating untraced/traced pairs, untraced first, of one task in one existing Chrome profile. Each run opens and closes its own background tab. All six attempts are included; none was re-run. Timing: first prediction after the initial homepage observation through the accepted DONE; setup and the independent post-run verification are excluded. The traced arm passes trace_path, so Agent.save() writes run.json twice per executed step.

gate.rule: traced median elapsed_ms within 10% of untraced median

summary.run_file_finding: In all three traced runs run.json ends with attempt set to an unexecuted step-11 WAIT and lacks the final DONE decision. The WAIT's pre-input save ran, Browser.act then raised StalePage, and the in-memory attempt was cleared without another save; DONE does not save. history matches state.json. run_goal's finish() saves once more, so MCP run files end with attempt null.
